BiblicalUsage: Widowhood, the state of being a widow, and the Bible uses it twice with opposite endings. Tamar puts off her widow's garments and covers herself with a veil, the dress of her widowhood laid aside for the plan that will get her justice. And the restored city is told she shall forget the shame of her youth, and shall not remember the reproach of her widowhood any more.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for widowhood carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the promise with it, that the reproach of widowhood is not the last word — God forgets what He has healed.
